title: Types of substances and bonds - 123 school
heading: Types of substances and bonds
intro: You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.question: Which bond holds the particles in a metal together?
Which particles move freely in a metal?
Why does copper conduct current even in the solid state?

answers.b: There are freely moving negative ions
answers.d: The covalent bonds let charge through

questions.question: Which property is typical for a metal?

answers.a: It does not conduct current in the solid state

questions.question: Why can you bend a copper wire without it breaking?

answers.a: The water molecules in the copper act as a lubricant
answers.b: The copper atoms share electrons and form molecules
answers.c: Ions with the same charge repel each other
answers.d: The layers of metal ions slide past each other and the free electrons keep them together

questions.question: What is an alloy?

answers.b: A mixture of a metal with other elements
answers.c: A molecule of two metal atoms

questions.question: Which of these elements is a metal? (use BINAS table 99)
Between which two kinds of atoms does an ionic bond form?
What happens to the electrons when sodium chloride forms from sodium and chlorine?

answers.a: Chlorine gives an electron to sodium
answers.b: The electrons become free and move through the lattice
answers.c: Sodium and chlorine share an electron pair
answers.d: Sodium gives an electron to chlorine

questions.question: Why is a salt crystal brittle?

answers.a: After a shift ions with the same charge sit next to each other and repel each other
answers.b: The molecules are only weakly bound to each other
answers.c: The ions can slide freely past each other
answers.d: The free electrons disappear when it is hit

questions.question: What does the formula NaCl mean for table salt?

answers.a: There are two Na<sup>+</sup> ions per Cl<sup>-</sup> ion
answers.b: There are molecules of one Na atom and one Cl atom
answers.c: There is one Cl<sup>-</sup> ion for each Na<sup>+</sup> ion
answers.d: Sodium and chlorine share an electron pair

questions.question: Which kind of substance is MgCl<sub>2</sub>?
Which kind of substance is Fe?
Which kind of substance is (NH<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>?
Which statement about a salt is correct?

answers.a: It consists of ions and is neutral as a whole
answers.b: It consists of ions and is positive as a whole
answers.c: It consists of molecules and is neutral as a whole
answers.d: It consists of atoms and free electrons

questions.question: Why does magnesium oxide (Mg<sup>2+</sup>, O<sup>2-</sup>) melt at a higher temperature than sodium chloride (Na<sup>+</sup>, Cl<sup>-</sup>)?

answers.a: The ions are smaller than molecules
answers.d: The ions have a larger charge and attract each other more strongly

questions.question: Which bond is broken when table salt melts?

answers.a: The covalent bond in the molecules
answers.b: The hydrogen bond between the molecules
answers.c: The ionic bond between the ions

questions.question: Why do molecular substances usually have a low melting point?

answers.a: They have no bonds at all
answers.c: Only the weak bonds between the molecules are broken
answers.d: The covalent bonds in the molecules break first

questions.question: A substance conducts current as a solid and as a liquid and does not dissolve in water. Which kind of substance is it?
A substance does not conduct current as a solid, but does when melted. Which kind of substance is it?
Which particles carry the charge in molten salt?
Which combination of kind of substance and typical bond is correct?
What happens when a salt dissolves in water?

answers.a: Water molecules pull the ions out of the lattice
answers.b: The ions are converted into molecules
answers.c: The electrons are shared with the water
answers.d: The salt melts because of the heat of the water
